apps.name: NekoSpeak
apps.sourceChannel: https://github.com/siva-sub/NekoSpeak/releases/download/v1.5.0/app-arm64-v8a-release.apk (official GitHub Release; asset size matches GitHub API exactly)
apps.framework: native Kotlin + Jetpack Compose (navigation-compose, material3); 1 classes.dex (arm64 asset); no DI framework; Gson; no analytics/ads SDKs
httpStack: no HTTP client library declared; model downloads via Android DownloadManager/workmanager-style code (VoiceDownloader.kt)
services: com.nekospeak.tts.NekoTtsService — exported=true, intent-filter android.intent.action.TTS_SERVICE, meta-data android.speech.tts -> @xml/tts_engine
apps.ttsArchitecture: It IS a system TTS engine: class NekoTtsService : TextToSpeechService() (NekoTtsService.kt:37). Engine strategy interface TtsEngine with PiperEngine (+EspeakWrapper -> libespeak-ng phonemes, 371 bundled espeak-ng-data assets), KokoroEngine (kokoro-v1.0.int8.onnx + voices-v1.0.bin), PocketTtsEngine (5 ONNX sessions: mimi_encoder 73MB, text_conditioner 16MB, flow_lm_main_int8 76MB, flow_lm_flow_int8 10MB, mimi_decoder_int8 23MB), Kitten TTS Nano. Kotlin Misaki G2P (engine/misaki/{G2P,Lexicon,Num2Words,TokenContext,MToken}.kt + piper/MisakiToPiperIPA.kt). Zero-shot cloning: cloneVoice() at PocketTtsEngine.kt:1526 with MimiCodec + GtcrnDenoiser + AudioRecorder/VoiceRecorderScreen.
apps.extractionApproach: none — it is a TTS engine, not a reader; there is no WebView, no article extraction, no book source
apps.playbackArchitecture: n/a (synthesis only, consumed by host apps through the system TTS binder); no MediaSession, no mediaPlayback FGS
apps.monetizationSignals: none — free open-source app, no billing code, no ad SDKs

apps.novelspeakComparison: Complementary rather than competing: NekoSpeak exposes itself as the device TTS engine via android.intent.action.TTS_SERVICE, whereas NovelSpeak bundles sherpa-onnx Kokoro/Pocket inside the app (README.md:11-12, SherpaEngine.kt). NovelSpeak could adopt the engine-export idea (become a system TTS provider) OR keep the in-app engine; NekoSpeak's model supply chain is split across GitHub releases, HF datasets and even an HF Space — the opposite of NovelSpeak's pinned-hash approach. NekoSpeak's support-report design is directly copyable.

denoiser preprocessing (GTCRN) before voice-clone embedding

apps.legalNotes: Open-source app under the MIT License (observed in repo LICENSE file: "Copyright (c) 2026 NekoSpeak Team"). Its ONNX models are third-party (Kyutai Pocket-TTS, HuggingFace Piper voices, Kokoro) with their own licences — do not copy weights. Architecture (TextToSpeechService + ONNX) is standard Android and freely re-implementable.
